info.title: biohub-cellmot-baseline
info.subtitle: Trained weights + patched code for the BioHub cell-tracking competition
info.description:
# Cell Tracking Baseline (UNet + Transformer)

A ready-to-run baseline for the [BioHub â€“ Cell Tracking During Development](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/biohub-cell-tracking-during-development) competition: cell detection and linking in 3D+time light-sheet microscopy with **sparse ground truth**. A short tracking demo (`assets/demo.gif`) and metric figures ship in the dataset files.

## What's inside

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `weights/baseline/split_0/edge_predictor_best.pth` | Trained joint detector + linker checkpoint (~8 MB). Same weights as the public [UNet baseline inference notebook](https://www.kaggle.com/code/thibautgoldsborough/unet-baseline-inference-submission); **not** trained to convergence â€” expect gains from training longer. |
| `weights/baseline/split_0/config.json` | Architecture config for the checkpoint (channels, layers, downsample, pool kernel). |
| `src/tracking_cellmot/` | Model definitions (`TemporalUNet3D`, `SimpleNodeTransformer`), the competition metric (`metrics.py`, `division_metrics.py`), and dataset IO. |
| `scripts/predict_unet_transformer.py` | Inference: detection + linking â†’ `.geff` graphs. Patched with `--edge-threshold`, `--pool-kernel-um`, `--max-children`, a split detection/linking path, and a parameter-free distance linker. |
| `scripts/linking.py` | Standalone linker: physical-distance gate, Hungarian assignment, constant-velocity motion model, single-frame gap closing. Pure array work, no GPU. |
| `scripts/train_unet_transformer.py` | Training with gate-aligned candidate sampling and `link_acc * test_recall` checkpoint selection. |
| `scripts/sweep_linkers.py`, `scripts/sweep_detection.py` | One detection pass per video, many linker / detector configs replayed on CPU. |
| `scripts/geffs_to_csv.py`, `scripts/csv_to_geffs.py` | Submission round-trip: `.geff` graphs â†” Kaggle submission CSV. |
| `scripts/evaluate.py` | Score predicted `.geff`s against ground-truth `.geff`s (no images loaded). |
| `tests/` | Metric unit tests and division sandbox examples. |
| `metrics.md` | The competition metric, explained with worked examples. |

## Quick start

```bash
uv sync
uv run python scripts/predict_unet_transformer.py --method baseline --split 0 \
  --edge-threshold 0.01 --pool-kernel-um 5.0 --max-children 1
uv run python scripts/evaluate.py \
  --pred-dir predictions/$USER/baseline/split_0 --gt-dir data/train
```

See `README.md` for the full training / prediction / submission workflow and the Python API.

## Gotchas worth knowing

- **Always pass `--edge-threshold` explicitly.** The upstream default (0.5) emits **zero edges** at inference density (~240 candidates/frame â†’ softmax â‰ˆ 0.004), and the metric then silently reports score `0.0` without running node matching.
- `--pool-kernel-um` quantises hard: it becomes `round(um / 1.625)` voxels forced odd, so 3.0 / 4.0 / 5.0 are all the same setting (kernel 3).
- Coordinates in the `.geff` files are **voxel indices** â€” scale by `(1.625, 0.40625, 0.40625)` Âµm/voxel before any distance reasoning.
- Score = `adjusted_edge_jaccard + 0.1 Ã— division_jaccard` â€” edges dominate 10:1.
- The classical-linker config above reaches roughly **0.74** on the public leaderboard; the neural edge score does not beat plain proximity once candidates are distance-gated.
